$description: Tier 1 · Global primitives. Raw values only. Emitted as --g-*. Never referenced by components directly; semantic tokens alias these. The neutral ramp, the accent ramps, white-alpha and the hue angles are legacy: apps alias them from their own layers, so they stay, unchanged, but no core role points at the neutral ramp any more (success, warning and info keep their accent ramps).

neutral.$description: Legacy neutral ramp (hue 260), kept unchanged for app layers that alias it. Not themed: the core reads the theme slots instead.

150.$description: Support text in dark mode (--support-foreground): Emphasis Engine's text level 4, between primary (neutral.25) and secondary (neutral.250) text, at least Lc 12 from each on every page surface.

250.$description: Secondary text in dark mode (--muted-foreground): Emphasis Engine's text level 3, Lc 79 on the page and Lc 77 on every dark fill (neutral.800, an input's fill), so it clears APCA Bronze everywhere and stays Lc 25 under primary text.

450.$description: Control borders in light mode (--input): 3.4:1 on white, over the 3:1 a field's edge needs (WCAG 1.4.11).

550.$description: Secondary text in light mode (--muted-foreground): Emphasis Engine's text level 3, the weakest step at APCA Lc 75 on every page surface it reads on (Lc 81 on white, 76 on neutral.50). No ramp step sat there: 500 is Lc 73 on white, 600 is 87. On a fill it gives way to neutral.600 (--muted-foreground-on-fill).

650.$description: Support text in light mode (--support-foreground): Emphasis Engine's text level 4, between primary (neutral.950) and secondary (neutral.550) text: Lc 95 on white, coded 10.5 under primary and 14 over secondary, so the three draw about 13 to 16 apart once small type is rendered.

blue.$description: Accent hues. 500 is the light-mode step, 400 the dark-mode step (lighter, so it keeps contrast on dark surfaces).

600.$description: Blue as text in light mode: Lc 75 or more on neutral.0, .50 and .100 (page, chrome, selected rows).

550.$description: The light-mode info fill (--info): the lightest blue that holds a white label at Lc 75 (it measures 76.3; 500 measures 72). Lc 60 or more as an ink on the stone grounds. Added at 1.0.

300.$description: Blue as text in dark mode: Lc 75 or more on neutral.950, .900 and .800.

50.$description: The light-mode running surface (--running-surface): blue.600 reads Lc 75 or more on it.

900.$description: The dark-mode running surface (--running-surface): blue.300 reads Lc 75 or more on it.

600.$description: Coral as text in light mode: Lc 75 or more on neutral.0, .50 and .100 (page, chrome, selected rows).

300.$description: Coral as text in dark mode: Lc 75 or more on neutral.950, .900 and .800.

600.$description: Green as text in light mode: Lc 75 or more on neutral.0, .50 and .100 (page, chrome, selected rows).

300.$description: Green as text in dark mode: Lc 75 or more on neutral.950, .900 and .800.

50.$description: The light-mode success surface (--success-surface): green.600 reads Lc 75 or more on it.

900.$description: The dark-mode success surface (--success-surface): green.300 reads Lc 75 or more on it.

600.$description: Amber as text in light mode: Lc 75 or more on neutral.0, .50 and .100 (page, chrome, selected rows).

550.$description: The light-mode warning fill (--warning): the lightest amber that holds a white label at Lc 75 (it measures 76.9). Lc 60 or more as an ink on the stone grounds, and Lc 45 or more as a solid against the ground, a raised surface, a selected row and a rule. Added at 1.0: no step sat there (500 holds white at Lc 49, 600 is a brown).

450.$description: The light-mode warning fill before 1.0: its label (neutral.950) Lc 62. --warning now uses amber.550 with a white label; kept unchanged for anything that points here.

300.$description: Amber as text in dark mode: Lc 75 or more on neutral.950, .900 and .800.

50.$description: The light-mode attention surface (--attention-surface): amber.600 reads Lc 75 or more on it.

900.$description: The dark-mode attention surface (--attention-surface): amber.300 reads Lc 75 or more on it.

700.$description: Destructive text in light mode: Lc 76 or more on neutral.0, .50 and .100 (a selected row), 75 on its own 10% tint.

600.$description: Destructive text in light mode for tokens 0.4-0.6 (Lc 84 on white, 74 on a selected row). --destructive now uses red.700; kept unchanged for anything that points here.

300.$description: Destructive text in dark mode for tokens 0.4-0.6 (Lc 76 on neutral.900, 74 on a selected row). --destructive now uses red.200; kept unchanged for anything that points here.

200.$description: Destructive text in dark mode: Lc 76 or more on neutral.950, .900 and .800 (a selected row), 72 on its own 20% tint.

white-alpha.$description: Translucent white, for hairlines on dark surfaces (shadcn's dark border/input). Alpha in the name is a percentage.

35.$description: Control borders in dark mode (--input): 3.1:1 or more on neutral.900 and neutral.950.

hue.$description: Bare hue angles for tinted surfaces. Lightness and chroma are semantic, so one hue gives a pastel wash in light mode and a deep one in dark.

theme.$description: Theme slots: the values that differ by app, one per Figma primitive, per ground (graphite = dark, stone = light). These are the defaults, Figma's default app (warpcore), so every slot exists with no data-theme attribute. tokens/themes/<app>.json re-declares all 28 under [data-theme="<app>"]. Tier 2 reads the stone slot in light and the graphite slot in dark; nothing else reads a slot.

needs-you.$description: Waiting on the person. One yellow and one near-black, the same in every app and both grounds (Figma needs-you/*, all 8 modes).

fill.$description: Figma needs-you/fill (VariableID:5:137); the <app>/<ground>/yel primitives all hold this value.

on-fill.$description: Figma needs-you/on-fill (VariableID:5:138); the <app>/<ground>/onYel primitives all hold this value.

critical.$description: Errors. One set per ground, the same for every app (Figma critical/*, typed into the Theme collection with no primitive behind it).

stone.$description: Figma critical/fill (VariableID:30:2325) in every stone mode.

swatch.$description: Twelve colours for things a person colours: calendars, notes, labels, personas, graph kinds (contract 5.1b #55). Evenly spaced OKLCH hues 30° apart, starting at the system's red hue angle (hue.red, 25). Each is solved per ground, the same for every app: the lightness that holds APCA Lc 62 (60, the floor for coloured text, plus 2) against the lowest-contrast of the eight surfaces it can sit on (surface-ground and surface-raised in all four apps), at a chroma of 0.14 on stone and 0.13 on graphite, or less where sRGB has no room at that lightness. So a swatch holds as text, and as a 2px bar, edge or mark (Lc 30) with room to spare. A swatch is a colour for data, never a status; it is never a fill behind text. Not in Figma.

scrim.$description: The full-screen dim behind sheets, dialogs and menus (Figma surface/scrim, VariableID:54:50), the same for every app. Graphite is opaque black; stone carries 64% alpha inside the colour, as Figma stores it. The layer's own opacity is a tier 3 knob (--c-scrim-sheet, -dialog, -menu): 0.5, 0.6 and 0.32 on graphite, 1 on stone, where this 64% is the whole dim.

graphite.$description: Figma surface/scrim (VariableID:54:50) in every graphite mode.

stone.$description: Figma surface/scrim (VariableID:54:50) in every stone mode: #141618 at 64% alpha.

base.$description: 2px: Figma radius/control (VariableID:7:31), the one corner every rounded part takes. Figma's radius/none (0) and radius/round (999) are Tailwind's own rounded-none and rounded-full.

size.$description: The two control sizes Figma holds as variables. Every other fixed size is a tier 3 knob of the component that draws it.

control.$description: 48px: Figma size/control (VariableID:27:1982). Every floating control, the tab bar, the status strip, a text field's least height.

touch-min.$description: 44px: Figma size/touch-min (VariableID:27:1983). The floor for a touch target.

stroke.$description: The two stroke widths the direction draws. Figma types them in; it has no stroke variable.

emphasis.$description: Focus and error borders, the selected-row edge, the tab indicator.

press.$description: A control going down under a finger or a click. The one step under 120ms: the hand is already there, so it must feel immediate.

state.$description: A surface changing state: a panel opening, a selection moving to a new place.

move.$description: Travel across the screen. The ceiling: no default motion runs longer.

tick.$description: One step of a countdown ring: a second, run linear, so the ring tracks the clock.

spin.$description: One turn of a spinner or a working ring.

pulse.$description: One beat of a pulse or a breathing halo: slow enough to read as alive, not alarming.

out.$description: Ease-out cubic: quick start, soft landing. Softer than standard.

in.$description: Ease-in cubic: slow start, fast finish. For things leaving.

in-out.$description: Ease-in-out cubic: for travel from one resting place to another.

back.$description: Overshoots to about 112% and comes back. For rare moments only.

pulse.$description: The even in-and-out of a pulse loop.

spring.$description: Damped springs at mass 1. Built to a CSS linear() curve that runs over the matching -duration token; the raw stiffness and damping are kept in tokens.json for JS. Each duration is the time the spring takes to stay within 1% of rest (scripts/check.mjs holds the two together).

settle.$description: A small thing arriving at a new place, with a slight overshoot (about 8%).

firm.$description: A large surface arriving. Under 3% overshoot, so it reads as physical with no visible bounce.

pop.$description: A clear bounce (about 20%). Expressive only: no core role points here.

step.$description: The delay between one sibling starting and the next.

max.$description: Siblings after this many start together, so the last one still lands inside the ceiling (4 steps of 50ms, then a 200ms entrance, is 400ms).

depth.$description: Scale of a pressed control of ordinary size (4% smaller).

depth-small.$description: Scale of a pressed icon-size control (10% smaller): a small target needs a larger change to show.

font.$description: Geist and Geist Mono, as values. @unicron/ui loads the font files (@fontsource-variable/geist, @fontsource-variable/geist-mono); the plain family name follows for an app that installs the static fonts.
